### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **42** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via validateExpression (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via validateExpression (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d498113b505f7b29b5e2c554f3152145edeb3461` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `391f8a88da1c686209b7ee31ea51915f367c3669` — the merge of head `5581ed26ee2e338a563eabf3b23f1ec1137f82be` into base `d498113b505f7b29b5e2c554f3152145edeb3461`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 391f8a88da1c686209b7ee31ea51915f367c3669 && git checkout 391f8a88da1c686209b7ee31ea51915f367c3669
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d498113b505f7b29b5e2c554f3152145edeb3461 5581ed26ee2e338a563eabf3b23f1ec1137f82be && git checkout -B drift-repro d498113b505f7b29b5e2c554f3152145edeb3461 && git merge --no-ff 5581ed26ee2e338a563eabf3b23f1ec1137f82be

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d498113b505f7b29b5e2c554f3152145edeb3461
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d498113b505f7b29b5e2c554f3152145edeb3461` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: 72/72 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5581ed26ee2e338a563eabf3b23f1ec1137f82be`

### ① Derived judgments
1. **Byte-identical messages: holds.** Own corpus, run through `tsx` against throwaway worktrees at `origin/main` (`569d4d2dbf`; the four producer files equal merge-base `de091b50e6`) and at head: 54,189 `validateExpression` calls (3 roles × ~740 inputs incl. non-string/bigint/symbol/function/Date/null-proto `source`, `ast`-only envelopes, nested/deep/oversized CEL, method calls, unknown functions, braces, templates, typos, roles, date/text/boolean arithmetic, traversal × 27 schema hints) → 28,674 errors + 438 warnings; 55 `collectCelRootIdentifiers` inputs (50 refusals); 50 slot values × `predicateSlotRefusal` / `structuralConditionRefusal` (75 refusals). Projection of `ok`/`message`/`source`/`error`/`roots`: **0 diffs**. Reading the diff confirms the CEL-compile arm's `bounds → method → unknownFn → braces → bare` fallthrough is order-equivalent to main's.
2. **Code sets: closed and complete.** `CODE_TABLE as const satisfies Record<Code, true>` (excess/missing key is a compile error) feeds `Object.freeze` lists; 21 formula + 4 spec. On my sweep every refusal carries a code from its own producer's set, all 25 codes are provoked, carriers are exactly `{code, message, params, source}` / `{ok, error, code, params}`, param key sets match the declared interfaces exactly (optional clauses present iff the sentence carries them; `limit`/`limitValue` paired; no `undefined` keys), every non-token param value is a substring of the message, `found`/`held` tokens cover every kind (`envelope`, `ast-without-source`, `object-without-source`, `bigint`, `symbol`, `function`…). All codes match `/^[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)+$/`; no leakage (`detail` is engine text already in the message, `limit` is the public `CelLimitKey`, lists are copies of caller input).
3. **Public surface: correct.** Formula root entry adds explicit named exports (package convention); spec's `automation/index.ts` is `export *`, so the 9 new names reach `@objectstack/spec/automation`; `api-surface/automation.json` and `export-origins/automation.json` gain exactly those 9, alphabetically placed with the right kinds; spec root does not re-export the file, so `root.json` is rightly untouched. `collectCelRootIdentifiers` `ok:false` arm: every reader in objectstack (lint ×4, objectql ×2, plugin-approvals, mcp) reads `.ok/.roots/.error`; objectui pin `rowPredicateCanon.ts:159` reads `.ok`; objectui main `requiredInGatedSection.ts:228` casts to a narrower `CollectRoots` and `screen-spec.ts:180` returns it through a narrower annotation — a `tsc` probe against head confirms both compile. No deep-equal or spread of any of the four results in either repo. `ExprValidationError` interface→alias: no `extends`/`implements`/constructor anywhere (grep hits only formula `index.ts`); objectui pin's local `FormulaModule` type and main's `optionLint.ts`/`flow-sim-validate.ts` read `.message` only.
4. **Pins: sound.** Mapped-type `PINS` over every code, runtime key equality, per-producer sweeps that must reach every code, spec partition test. My `tsc` probe: code-less literals rejected on all four carriers, unknown code rejected, foreign params rejected, narrowing on `code` narrows `params`. A new `errors.push({source,message})` or a new `{ok:false,error}` arm is red at typecheck; a new table key without a pin is red at the test's mapped type.
5. **Changeset: every sentence true**, `minor` for both, `Clause-②: yes` alone on line 14. MCP `validate_expression` forwards `errors`/`warnings` verbatim (`mcp-http-tools.ts:688`), so that sentence holds.
6. **Hand-off: accurate.** objectui main `flow-sim-validate.ts:162` is `structuralConditionRefusal(condition)` in `evalGuard`, `:163` shows `shape.message`; test `:128` asserts `STRUCTURAL_CONDITION_SHAPE_REFUSAL`; `tFormat` takes `Record<string, string | number>`; the no-hint code list matches `screen-spec.ts` and `evalCelPredicate` (both call with no schema). Non-blocking body inaccuracy: the consumer census says the pinned objectui's `screen-spec.ts`/`flow-sim-validate.ts` call the producers; at `f8a9d0fb05` neither imports `@objectstack/formula`/`spec` — the pin's readers are `celAuthoring.ts:502` and `rowPredicateCanon.ts:159`. Conclusion unchanged.

### ② Semver level
`minor` for `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/spec` is right. Per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `Clause-②: yes` with no arm reads as a widening that takes at least `minor`; the diff adds exported fields, types and two frozen lists and removes/renames nothing. The required `code`/`params` on result types could only bite a consumer that constructs or extends those values, and none exists in objectstack or objectui (pin or main), so no `(narrowing)` arm is warranted. CI `Check Changeset` green at head.

### ③ Boundary flags
- NOT-MEASURED packages (mcp, service-automation, objectql, plugin-approvals): covered by CI at head — `Type Check · workspace` (`turbo run typecheck --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'`) and `Test Core (1/6…6/6)` (`turbo run test`, whole workspace partitioned by package), all `success`; 42 check-runs read, 0 failures, 5 `skipped` by path filter (incl. Console Pin Gate; `.objectui-sha` unchanged).
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main 5581ed26ee` against current `origin/main` `569d4d2dbf`: clean, tree `1600ba698e`, exit 0.
